title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X is a compact curve of genus g ≥ 2 over C, and ω (underlined) is the canonical sheaf. E is the rank-2 bundle P^1_{X/S}(ω)⊗ω^{-1}, the twisted bundle of first-order principal parts. It is the unique non-split extension 0 → ω → E → O_X → 0, with extension class c ≠ 0 in H^1(X,ω) ≅ C; this is the Gunning bundle. P_X = P(E) is the associated ruled surface, and σ is the section given by the line subbundle ω. Every projective connection on X gives a flat P^1-bundle (a G-bundle, G = PGL_2) whose underlying bundle is P_X. Grothendieck is asking whether the map M_conn(X) → M_g^Γ(X) (projective connections → flat PGL_2-bundles / holonomy) is injective. In other words: can two different projective connections on the same X give isomorphic flat bundles? The question reduces to the automorphisms of P_X and how they act.

Step 1 (end of previous page, start of this one). An X-automorphism of P(E) comes from a line bundle L and an isomorphism E ≅ E⊗L. Taking determinants gives L^2 ≅ O_X. Consider the composite ω → E ≅ E⊗L → L. It is a section of ω^{-1}⊗L, which has negative degree ('L⊗ω^{-1} est anti-ample'), so it vanishes. Hence ω maps into ω⊗L, and any automorphism fixes the section σ.

Step 2. The induced map O_X → L on quotients must be an isomorphism, so L ≅ O_X. The automorphism therefore lifts to an automorphism u of E with u(ω) ⊂ ω. After normalising, u induces the identity on E/ω ≅ O_X. Let λ ∈ H^0(O_X^*) = C^* be the scalar u induces on ω. Compatibility with the extension class gives λc = c, so (λ−1)c = 0. Since c ≠ 0, λ = 1.

Step 3. So u is an automorphism of the extension, i.e. u = id + (E → O_X → ω → E), given by a holomorphic differential. Grothendieck concludes Aut_X(P_X) = Aut_X(P_X, σ) ≅ H^0(X, ω_X) as groups (additive), via u_ω ↔ ω.

Step 4. The injectivity question becomes: can u_ω carry the curve C ⊂ P_X (equivalently, the oper-type connection) attached to one projective connection to that of another, or fix it? The next page answers this by an explicit gauge computation in a local uniformiser t. There u_ω = exp θ_ω acts on the connection ^cD_t, and the difference u_ω(^cD_t) − ^cD_t is computed as a quadratic differential (terms in λ', λ^2 with ω = λ dt).

In modern terms: the unipotent radical of the Borel gauge group, i.e. Aut(Gunning bundle) = H^0(K) ≅ C^g, acts on PGL_2-opers on X. The page sets up the proof that holonomy restricted to a fixed Riemann surface is injective on projective structures. Equivalently, opers have no non-trivial automorphisms, and distinct opers on X give non-isomorphic flat bundles.
errors: No real error. The argument needs g ≥ 2 (deg ω^{-1}⊗L < 0, and dim H^1(ω) = 1 with c ≠ 0); this is implicit in the context.
The normalisation to the identity on the quotient E/ω uses the fact that projective automorphisms are only defined up to scalars; this is tacit but harmless.
The final question is left open on this page; the decisive computation is on the next page and is itself unfinished there.

ideas.what: Any automorphism of the ruled surface P(E) of the Gunning bundle fixes the section given by the destabilising subbundle ω, because Hom(ω, L) = 0 for L torsion.
ideas.modern_name: Uniqueness of the maximal destabilising subbundle / the oper section
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967); Loray–Marín (2009) in the ruled-surface language

ideas.what: Aut_X(P(E)) ≅ H^0(X, K) ≅ C^g as an additive group, acting by unipotent extension automorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism group of the Gunning ruled surface / unipotent Borel gauge group of opers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical folklore; explicit in Loray–Marín, 'Projective structures and projective bundles over compact Riemann surfaces' (Astérisque 2009)

ideas.what: Reducing injectivity of the projective-connection → flat-PGL_2-bundle map on a fixed curve to whether H^0(K) gauge transformations can identify two connections or sections.
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of the holonomy map on fibers of the bundle of projective structures over Teichmüller space; opers have no automorphisms (Drinfeld–Sokolov slice)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré/Hejhal tradition); Kapovich, Gallo–Kapovich–Marden (2000) for the proper embedding of fibers; Beilinson–Drinfeld for opers

missed.claim: This is an early, purely algebraic (EGA-style principal parts) treatment of projective connections as connections on the Gunning bundle P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)) with a distinguished section. It isolates the C^g = H^0(ω) unipotent gauge group, a precursor of the oper / Drinfeld–Sokolov viewpoint. The result itself (injectivity of holonomy on a fixed curve; triviality of oper automorphisms) is known in the literature.
missed.quote: Donc Aut_X(P_X) = Aut_X(P_X, σ) ≃ H^0(X, ω_X) ... La question est donc la suivante: Peut-on avoir u_ω(C) = C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents that Grothendieck treated projective structures relatively over a base S with flat-bundle moduli M_g^Γ(X), in a form close to the later oper formalism. No new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The argument is correct and cleanly algebraic, and it anticipates the oper / Gunning-bundle viewpoint. But the facts (automorphisms of the Gunning ruled surface form H^0(K); holonomy is injective on a fixed complex structure) are known and published by others.
